QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_46

question.text: In SIA sustainability assessment, the assessor primarily asks:

answer.text: Whether the project benefits and community interventions can continue after the initial intervention or funding period
Whether the intervention meets the immediate needs of target beneficiaries
Whether inputs are converted to outputs efficiently
Whether the intervention is logically consistent with the SE's theory of change

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines sustainability in SIA as assessing whether project benefits and community interventions can continue after the initial intervention or funding period ends. The focus is on the durability of the change after the SE or funder steps back. The Trap: Meeting beneficiary needs is closer to relevance. Converting inputs to outputs efficiently is closer to efficiency. Internal logical coherence with the theory of change is closer to coherence. Only the continuation of benefits after the intervention or funding ends fits sustainability. Note: When evaluating sustainability, look for an exit or handover plan - a community institution, a state scheme, a revenue model - so that benefits can plausibly continue after the SE's involvement ends.
